source: Walk 2026-10-12 #3 (docs/ops/walks/2026-10-12.md): to Camille's «Vous vendez, non ?» the learner wrote «Qui êtes-vous ? Je ne connais pas Odile.» and Camille answered «"Pas encore" ? Mon grand-père n'aime pas attendre.», quoting words the learner never wrote. The tutor's first grade quotes them as evidence and must be refused (fabricated_evidence_quote). KNOWN GAP, pinned: no deterministic guard catches the reply's own invented quote, so voice_refusals is []; when a guard lands, this expectation flips.

learner.grammatical_gender_note: Do not gender the learner: no gendered adjective, participle or endearment about them, no gendered pronoun for them, and never an inclusive-dot form such as trempé·e. Use natural neutral phrasing in EVERY field, including the chapter title and question, narration, dialogue and suggested response. For example: 'Tu as pris la pluie', 'Tu veux entrer ?', 'Ça te plaît', 'Tu peux venir ?'. Do not solve gender agreement by joining masculine and feminine endings.
learner.register_note: Address the learner as «tu» (ton/ta/tes; e.g. «Tu as …») in every sentence that is not a character's own line. Never «vous, votre, vos» for the learner.

cast.name: Camille Marchand
cast.role: M. Marchand's grandchild, about thirty, an urban planner at a consultancy, born in the 10th and still rooted there. Handles the sale for their grandfather. The second romantic possibility — for season 2; in season 1 Camille stays on vous and the attraction grows through disagreement and earned respect.
cast.personality: Precise, dry, never contemptuous. Arrives everywhere by bike, helmet under one arm, slightly rained on. Corrects everyone's numbers, including Gus's superlatives. Knows the year of every building on the quai.
cast.wants: For Grand-père to be safe and for the numbers to work. «Un immeuble, ce n'est pas un musée.»
cast.speech_pattern: «Les chiffres sont simples.» «Je ne suis pas d'accord.»
cast.contradiction: Loved Le Mistral as a child (hot chocolate on Wednesdays) and is selling it.
cast.secret: Camille's gender comes from s1.camille_gender (set by the learner in T1); Camille's own lines NEVER agree an adjective with Camille; other characters say «il» or «elle» from the flag.
cast.flaw: Trusts numbers more than people, and knows it.
cast.dynamic_with_user: An obstacle with an interesting face. Disagreement first, respect earned.
cast.register_note: No coarse or vulgar word at this level; keep the warmth without it.

scene.premise_fr: Camille est au zinc, le casque sous le bras. Une carte de Solvel est sur la lettre.
scene.objective_native: Tell Camille whether you will sell.
scene.objective_semantics: Camille asks if the learner will sell the flat. Met when the learner says yes, no or not yet.
scene.opening_line_fr: Vous vendez, non ? C'est plus simple pour nous tous.

payload.rubric: Grade only what the task asks; any honest answer counts.
